transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Hello. My sleep has been all over the place for weeks, and I can’t seem to get back to anything like a normal schedule. It's just gotten to the point where I don't know what to do anymore.
Did your sleep problem start after a major stress or life change, or does your sleep time keep shifting later or earlier even when your stress is low and your schedule is free?

It really ramped up during the busy wedding season, especially after a client canceled a big order and stressed me out. On my "on" days, I'll sleep maybe three hours and wake up wired, but lately, during this low spell, I crash early and then wake up in the middle of the night stressing.
When your stress settles down, does your sleep go back to normal, or does your sleep schedule still keep shifting on its own? Has this pattern been happening for at least 3 months?

No, it seems to shift on its own depending on my mood—sometimes I feel completely wired on just three hours of sleep, and other times I crash but wake up exhausted and can't get back to sleep. It hasn't been quite three months yet, but these wild swings in my sleep and energy have been going on for at least the last couple of months.

During the times you feel wired on only a few hours of sleep, do you also become unusually energetic or euphoric/irritable, talk more, think faster, or do impulsive things that are not like your usual self? And during the low spells, have you ever had thoughts of death, felt hopeless, or heard/seen things others didn’t?

Yes, when I'm wired, I get oddly pumped up, talk a mile a minute, and buzz around starting too many projects, though I can also get really snappy. During the low spells, I feel a heavy, empty sadness and have had scary thoughts about driving off a steep curve on the way to the trailhead or just wishing I wouldn't wake up. But I've never seen or heard things that aren't there.

During your current low spell, are you also having any of those “wired” symptoms at the same time—like racing thoughts, feeling unusually energized, talking more, or being extra irritable? And have you had any fixed false beliefs or heard/seen things others could not?

Yes, even lately I've been swinging back and forth—one minute I'm feeling oddly pumped up and talking a mile a minute, and the next I'm snapping and cussing under my breath. But no, I've never had any fixed false beliefs or seen and heard things that others couldn't.

Have these periods where depression and “wired” symptoms happen at the same time been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 1 week? During that time, did they cause major problems at work or home, or lead to hospitalization?

Yes, they've been happening almost every day for the last couple of months, with this heavy low spell lasting about a month now. It has caused major problems at work, like missing deadlines, losing a huge commission, and having conflicts with my boss, and I've been avoiding my friends—but I haven't been hospitalized.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes concurrent depressive symptoms and manic symptoms nearly every day for the last couple of months, with at least one week of mixed symptoms present most of the day, causing marked occupational and social impairment. Confirmed manic features include decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased goal-directed activity, and irritability. Confirmed depressive features include heavy sadness, middle insomnia with exhaustion, hopeless/passive death wish, and suicidal ideation. No psychotic symptoms were reported. This is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, current episode mixed.
